comments.text: The part that surprised me: the 2014 ruling at The Hague moved a big block of Pacific fishing water, but nobody ever asked the court about the land. So a few hectares of beach near Arica are still claimed by both countries, because the 1929 Treaty of Lima said the border starts at "a point on the coast" and Peru reads that as the waterline at Punto Concordia while Chile reads it as marker Hito 1, slightly inland. Sources are in the description. Is there a border near you that looks settled on a map but is argued over on the ground?
